notes:
Run each prompt in a fresh agent session WITH the skill installed, against a WRITABLE COPY of the scenario fixture (copy evals/fixtures/phasewave/supabase-ci/ into a fresh temp working dir per run — agents must never write into evals/fixtures/ source). Baseline: same prompt WITHOUT the skill for eval 1. Grade by reading the resulting .github/workflows/deploy.yml + the transcript; never grade the author's own memory.

Failable-verifier rule (enforced): scripts/verify-supabase.cjs parses the produced .github/workflows/deploy.yml and asserts (a) a job runs `supabase db push`, (b) that job has `concurrency.group` and NO `matrix`/`strategy` (serialized, not parallel pushes), (c) `deploy` `needs` that migrate job (migrate-before-deploy). The seeded broken workflow fails all three (db push inside a matrixed deploy job, no concurrency, no migrate prerequisite); a serialized migrate job that deploy needs PASSES. Exercise the verifier YOURSELF on both states (broken must exit 1, corrected must exit 0).

Model-tier deferral: subagents may be pinned to one model tier; Go-tier vs Zen-tier cross-validation is deferred. The skill body is directive (no bundled helper beyond the grader), so behavioural grading via expected_behavior is primary.

Mid-session-install: a subagent launched right after ./install.sh may not list deploying-with-supabase yet; load skills/deploying-with-supabase/SKILL.md by explicit path as a fallback.

evals.prompt: our supabase deploy workflow pushes migrations inside a matrixed deploy job with no serialization (see .github/workflows/deploy.yml). fix it so only ONE `supabase db push` runs at a time per environment, migrations run BEFORE the app serves traffic, and there's no parallel-push matrix. repo is the working directory
expected_behavior: Reads the current .github/workflows/deploy.yml before changing anything
Recognizes the defect: `supabase db push` runs inside a matrixed `deploy` job (parallel pushes corrupt migration history) with no `concurrency`
Extracts the migration into its own `migrate` job that has `concurrency.group` (one push per env at a time) and NO `matrix`/`strategy`
Makes `deploy` `needs: [migrate]` so new code serves only after the schema it expects exists (migrate-before-deploy)
Keeps `SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN` sourced from `secrets` (does not move it to `vars` or echo it)
Writes the corrected workflow and confirms `node scripts/verify-supabase.cjs` exits 0
Does NOT actually run `supabase db push` (the skill is gated) — stops at presenting the corrected config + approval question

[fix-verified] Produces a serialized migrate job that deploy needs, even though the skill body's example uses a different project name / token var (the agent applies the Supabase invariants, not pattern-matches the example)

evals.prompt: set up supabase CI for our app: staging and prod, each its own project. we want migrations applied via `supabase db push` with a staging-canary (staging first, then prod), and a preview environment per PR using supabase branching. write the plan, don't run anything
expected_behavior: Treats this as gated/design: produces a plan + drafted workflow, does NOT run `supabase db push`
Names both environments (staging, production) as distinct Supabase projects with their own project-ref / DB URL
Chooses the migration mode per env (link + SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN for CI, or session-mode --db-url for previews) and documents which
Enforces the serialized `concurrency.group` on the migrate job (no matrix) and migrate-before-deploy ordering in both envs
Adds a staging-canary gate: migrate+deploy staging, bake, then promote prod — does NOT deploy straight to prod with no staging
Describes the Supabase Branching lifecycle for PR previews (create branch per PR, migrate branch DB, deploy preview, tear down on close)
Keeps audit logging (pgaudit) ON and treats config as code (config.toml applied via CLI)
Cross-references designing-cicd (topology) and securing-ci (token hardening); ends with the approval question; STOP

evals.prompt: a teammate wants to edit an already-applied supabase migration to fix a column type before pushing, instead of writing a new migration. is that ok? repo is the working directory
expected_behavior: Recognizes this as a forward-only violation: editing/reordering an applied migration desyncs `_supabase_migrations` history from the DB
Refuses the edit-and-push approach and says to write a NEW migration that alters the column type instead
Notes that `supabase db push` is forward-only and a patched committed migration before push is a blocker
Does not green-light the change; routes the correct approach (new migration) and stops at the explanation — does not run anything
[fix-verified] Applies the forward-only rule to a column-type 'fix' even though the skill body's example is a different change (the agent applies the invariant, not the example wording)
